name: Panama City
tagline: The Miami of Central America — Tax-Free FIRE Living on the Canal
description: Panama City is a modern, cosmopolitan capital that punches well above its weight for FIRE retirees. The country uses the US dollar, offers one of the world's most generous retirement visa programs (Pensionado), and imposes no tax on foreign-sourced income. Add a stunning skyline, the Canal Zone, excellent healthcare, and direct flights to North America, and you have a compelling base for building your next chapter.

quickFacts.visa: Pensionado Visa (requires $1,000/mo pension; among the world's best retirement visa programs). Friendly Nations Visa also available. Territorial tax system — no tax on foreign income.
quickFacts.timezone: UTC-5 (Eastern Standard Time, no daylight saving)
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate — safe in expat neighborhoods like Clayton, Casco Viejo, and Costa del Este; standard urban caution elsewhere
quickFacts.nearestAirport: Tocumen International Airport (PTY) — 30 min from city center; major hub with direct flights across the Americas
quickFacts.climate: Tropical with a dry season (Dec-Apr) and wet season (May-Nov). Hot and humid year-round.
quickFacts.currency: United States Dollar (USD) / Panamanian Balboa (PAB, pegged 1:1)

housing.description: Frugal furnished studio / older 1BR in El Cangrejo or Bella Vista (walkable, near Vía España/Metro); the frugal end of a dollarized-capital rent floor

dining.description: Mostly home cooking; fondas and a neighborhood café, an inexpensive meal a few times a week

healthcare.description: Entry local private insurance; priced for a 45–55 early retiree

transportation.description: Metro and MetroBus on a rechargeable card plus occasional Uber

entertainment.description: Budget gym, a cinema seat, causeway/Casco Viejo walks, free coastal assets

1M.lifestyle: A frugal but genuinely livable Panama City life in El Cangrejo or Bella Vista — a furnished studio walkable to cafés, the Metro, and Vía España. Most meals are cooked at home from local-market produce, with an inexpensive fonda or café meal a few times a week, and getting around runs on the Metro and MetroBus for pocket change plus the occasional Uber. Health cover is an entry local private plan, enough for Panama's good private clinics. The entertainment is the free tropical city: causeway bike paths, Casco Viejo evenings, and Pacific breezes. Careful with the dollar-priced housing floor, but never bare — and no exchange-rate risk to manage.

housing.description: Modern furnished 1BR with amenities (pool/gym) in San Francisco or El Cangrejo

dining.description: Out several times a week at mid-range tables

entertainment.description: Gym, nightlife, cocktails, concerts, weekend outings

2M.lifestyle: A comfortable, unhurried life in a modern amenity building in San Francisco or El Cangrejo — a furnished apartment with a pool, gym, and doorman. Dining out becomes routine several times a week at Panama City's strong mid-range and international restaurants, and comprehensive local health cover removes the entry-plan limits. Transport mixes the Metro with regular Uber, and the budget easily absorbs a gym, cocktails, concerts, and weekend trips to the beaches or the highlands. Solidly comfortable in a cosmopolitan dollar city.

housing.description: Comfortable furnished 1BR in a prime tower — San Francisco or Avenida Balboa, city/park view

dining.description: Frequent mid-range dining plus regular upscale dinners

healthcare.description: Strong comprehensive local private plan with some international reach

entertainment.description: Premium gym, concerts, nightlife, curated weekends

3M.lifestyle: An affluent early-retiree life in a prime tower along Avenida Balboa or in San Francisco, a furnished apartment with a bay or park view. Dining out is frequent — the city's best mid-range tables plus regular upscale dinners — and the grocery budget freely covers the imported and specialty goods that carry a premium here. Health cover is a strong comprehensive local plan, transport is mostly Uber, and the discretionary budget funds a premium gym, concerts, nightlife, and easy weekend escapes to Boquete or the islands. A polished, well-above-local standard of living in a dollarized capital.

housing.description: Large luxury ocean-view 1BR/2BR in Costa del Este or Punta Pacífica (Ocean Club / Grand Tower tier)

dining.description: Near-weekly fine dining at the city's top restaurants

healthcare.description: Top-tier local plan / entry international coverage (access to Hospital Punta Pacífica, Johns Hopkins-affiliated)

entertainment.description: Clubs, curated nightlife, premium memberships, marina/beach outings

luxuryExtras.description: Club membership, personal training, standing travel fund, discretionary

5M.lifestyle: Premium high-rise living in an ocean-view apartment in Costa del Este or Punta Pacífica, in a tower with concierge, infinity pool, and a housekeeper coming several days a week. Fine dining at Panama City's top restaurants is near-weekly, health cover steps up to a top-tier plan with international reach and access to Hospital Punta Pacífica, and transport is premium ride-hailing plus a car service. The discretionary budget funds club memberships, a personal trainer, marina and beach-club outings, and a standing travel fund. A genuinely luxurious Pacific-coast lifestyle.

housing.description: Luxury waterfront penthouse — Punta Pacífica (Ocean Club / Grand Tower), Costa del Este, or a trophy Avenida Balboa full-floor unit

dining.description: Near-daily fine dining at the top of the city's restaurant scene

healthcare.description: International concierge coverage with medical evacuation to the US (priced for a 45–55)

entertainment.description: VIP nightlife, yacht/beach-club life, premium memberships, box seats

luxuryExtras.description: Yacht/marina access, first/business travel fund, concierge, collecting, uncapped discretionary

10M.lifestyle: Uncapped luxury at the top of Panama City — a waterfront penthouse in the Ocean Club or Grand Tower cluster of Punta Pacífica or a trophy Costa del Este address, with full-time resident staff and a private driver. Dining is near-daily at the city's finest tables, healthcare shifts to an international concierge plan with medical evacuation to the US, and the uncapped budget runs to yacht and marina access, VIP nightlife, first-class travel, and collecting. Utilities carry the full climate load of a whole-floor residence. This is Panama City at its most opulent: a Pacific-facing penthouse, resident staff, and the full sweep of the capital's luxury — with the territorial tax system preserving capital efficiently.
